items.briefing:
Australian businesses are being warned of a rise in Business Email Compromise (BEC) scams, where criminals impersonate executives or suppliers to trick staff into transferring money or sharing sensitive information. These scams are particularly convincing because they often use real company details and appear to come from trusted contacts. Separately, users of AI tools like Anthropic's Claude have been targeted by information-stealing attacks that hijack active login sessions, meaning attackers can access accounts without needing a password.

If you receive an unexpected email requesting a payment, account change, or login — even from a familiar name — verify it by phone before acting.

featured.title: PhishByte warns of rising BEC scams hitting Australian firms
featured.summary: Australian firms are being urged to tighten payment checks as email impersonation scams drive AUD $166.8 million in losses.
